title: Suburban Gardens personnel and Charlie Margulis's visit for the Edsel
summary: Band members, Charlie Margulis's high-note playing and his advice about trumpet longevity, and his visit in 1957 for Ford's Edsel launch.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I played drums, yeah. And, uh, did you play any piano, Jose? Yeah, I played piano, played piano, and drums, and, that was, uh, let's see, we had, Pinky was there, Mark Smith, uh, I don't remember who was playing, I don't remember who was playing first alto. We had quite a conglomeration of musicians there. Ray Bonitas was playing, he was playing string bass, we had a player, we had a bass player by the name of Finats. Yeah. An Italian player, Finats. Yeah. I know, I know his son. And then, Bobby Castigliola's father was there for a while, and he wanted a, he wanted a Charlie Margulis, high trumpet player, and then he says, I, Shaniowski says, I sent to the union to get a Charlie Margulis and they sent me this, he can't even hit C. Charlie Margulis, he was the first guy that started hitting high notes, he was with White in the orchestra. In fact, Charlie Margulis was in his house already. In fact, I got an autograph from him that, now you'll laugh when I tell you why he was down here. The year that we introduced the automobile that Ford Motor Company put out, which was the biggest flop that they ever made. Charlie came down here with another fellow who was later the manager of the Baltimore Symphony. The day, when we introduced in 1957, this automobile. No, no, it's a Ford. This is a Ford, this is the one they named after the song? Edsel. Edsel, oh. Edsel. The one that I did was to play a trumpet. And they came down here to. I had the orchestra for it. And they sent down the key men. The drummer and the trumpet player and the piano player. And all I did was manage the thing. In fact, I was working at the radio station there. And that's when Charlie Margulis used to come in there and listen to Al Hurd play. He says he's got to make it. He says he can't make it just playing trumpet. He says he's got to do something else or he'll poop himself out. He says he can play, but he can't play that much. He says he's got to learn how to do something a little other than playing trumpet because you won't last that long with what he tries to do. And it's very true. I mean, you can't stand up and play high notes all day long and last any length of time. So you've got to either learn how to sing or to talk or to do something. And that's when Charlie Margulis was down here. He had a great admiration for Howard. Charlie was the beginning of the high note arts with Weitner. How was Venantz? Venantz was a very fine, legitimate bass player. Very fine. He was a very typical Italian, get mad in a hurry. And he was in very, very fast temperament.
You ought to see his son. He looks just like him. Is that right? I've seen the picture.
